summary: Computed L_C(p)=#{u>=1:(4uC-1)|(p+u)} (trial form of (★), FRONTIER §2.1) for all primes p≡1 (4), p≤10^6 (39175 primes), C=2^j, j=0..10 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_lev.c; analysis scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_z2911_an.py). Marginal level-failure rates rise 0.24 (C=1) to 0.999 (C=1024). Joint failure over j<k is 0.75–0.91× the independent product (all 11 levels: 1918 vs 2098 expected); adjacent-level phi ≈ −0.14 (C=1,2), −0.10, −0.07, but C=1 vs C=4 is +0.17. Same deficit for p>10^5 (fail j≤4: 1734 vs 1942 indep), so it is not a small-prime artefact; the effect is modest and the marginals are p-averaged, so no lottery-type conclusion is drawn.
not_done: Only p≤10^6 (spec was 10^8: cost ~100x per 10x p); no conditioning on the level-C residue of p beyond p mod 8; no comparison with a per-prime (p-conditioned) null model.

summary: Tested the e-slice pigeonhole (|Div(N1)|+|Div(N2)| > φ(e) with N1=(p+e)/4, N2=(pe+1)/4, Div = residues mod e of divisors) for the 9 (★)-failing primes ≤10⁶ and 4 controls, e≤3000 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z2920.py; out z2920_out.txt). The criterion fires only for small e (largest firing e: 71 at p=83449, 35 at p=712321; ratio max 1.2–2.0 at e∈{3,7,11,…}), it pairs divisors of two different cofactors so it does not produce a certificate of a single slice, and exact single-N certificates exist at 8–66 slices per prime anyway, with ratio <1. The 'forces a certificate' step therefore does not follow.
not_done: Did not extend beyond e≤3000 or p≤10⁶; did not test the variant with N1=N2 (not defined in the item).
next: If the item is kept, rewrite the pigeonhole with a single cofactor N and sets {a mod e: a|N} to get a genuine slice criterion, then test it.

summary: Lemma (verified exactly on all 7.8·10⁶ pairs (p,C), p≤10⁶, C≤200): the number of divisors d≡−1 (mod 4C) of 4Cp+1 is odd iff 4Cp+1 is a square s² with s≡−1 (mod 4C) (involution d↔N/d). Hence R(p)=Σ_C L_C(p) is always even and the parity is forced only at square levels. The natural non-forced quantity is the half-count H(p)=R(p)/2: its parity is balanced (19571 odd vs 19603 even, p≤10⁶; scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z2990.py). So the naive parity is trivial and the non-trivial parity is free.
not_done: Half-count parity per level H_C was not tabulated separately (only the total R/2 mod 2); no Rédei-type predictor tested.
next: Test whether R(p)/2 mod 2 correlates with a Rédei/genus symbol of 4Cp+1 for the same levels.

summary: Checked the quaternion-order material (BRAINSTORM/gon_fermat_certificates.md §(iii): maximal orders in B_{p,∞}, Minkowski route). summary: BM_CORRECTED_COUNT.md §2 already gives M_BM(p) ≥ (3/(16π²)−o(1))L² via Burgess and ≥(1/(32π²)−o(1))L² via Pólya–Vinogradov (line 105); a Siegel bound would replace Burgess only in the constant and make it ineffective, so the M_BM ≫ (log p)² statement stays unconditional and the all-large-p consequence still needs the lower tail R(p) ≥ εM_BM(p) (H⁻_BM, §3, which is equivalent to (★) for p>p₀ by line 171). Siegel therefore yields an ineffective version of a quantity that is already unconditional, not an all-large-p theorem.
